description: We are NovaChrono, a team made up of aspiring engineers brought together by a common mission which is to explore new ideas, create , develop and build impactful technology.
summary: Welcome to Stranded on Mars: Seven Sols! For the NASA Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge, we built a survival mission powered by real space science. Meet Muntasir and Maisha, two astronauts who crash-land on Mars, with messages to Earth taking up to twenty minutes. With no one to ask, they must run their outpost alone, balancing power, oxygen, water and radiation across seven days. Along the way, they face dust-covered solar panels, shrinking ice, and a solar storm, based on real NASA records from May 2024 and radiation measured by the Curiosity rover. But this isn’t just a story, it’s you in action. As the player, you step into their boots and take on hands-on tasks where no choice is free: power for oxygen leaves less for the night, and stepping outside in a storm drains your radiation shield. Make a wrong move and the trainer pauses, shows you the science, and lets you rewind. Keep track of each days journey and teachings based on real NASA data everyday. This is NASA science like you’ve never seen it before, not in charts or reports, but as a playful, high-stakes mission in your browser as a game.
details:
Space lessons for kids are usually either too simple, like posters, or too hard to follow. Kids see how a space mission ends, but never the decisions behind it. Our game lets them make those decisions themselves.

In Stranded on Mars: Seven Sols, two astronauts, Muntasir and Maisha, crash-land on Mars, and the player helps them survive for seven sols. Each day brings a new problem. Dust covers the solar panels, the oxygen runs low, the water runs out, and a solar storm is on the way. The player walks around the outpost and the Martian surface and solves each problem with small mini-games, like cleaning a panel, drilling for ice or switching things off. No choice is free. Making oxygen uses power, for example, so there is less power left for everything else. Four meters for power, oxygen, water and radiation show what each choice costs, and they appear one at a time so nothing feels overwhelming.

A wrong choice is never the end. The game pauses, rewinds and shows a real NASA fact about what went wrong, so kids learn from mistakes without being punished. Each day also adds a page to a logbook with real NASA photos and facts, and every fact shows where it came from. We will use NASA open Data from DONKI, OSDR and Curiosity mission for all the purposes. The numbers on the meters are made up for the game and are not NASA measurements.

The game runs in any web browser with no download and no account.

AI tools used: Antigravity CLI for necessary code formatting/debugging

Coding languages: JavaScript, HTML, Phaser.js, Vite.js

Softwares used: Autodesk Sketchbook(for drawing game components), Piskel( for animating sprite)
